gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Jackery rates the Explorer 1000 v2 for 4,000 cycles to 70% of capacity, while Anker rates the C1000 Gen 2 for 4,000 cycles and BLUETTI rates the AC180 for 3,500 cycles, both to 80%. None states that the Jackery and the AC180 take 20 ms to switch to battery in an outage, against under 10 ms for EcoFlow's DELTA 3 Classic.
standout_why: I read four pages. Lights On Labs (cited, 2026-10-27), PowerSized's kit price guide (cited, 2026-10-17) and StormWatts' same-panel-watts comparison (cited, 2026-11-08) give capacity, one output figure, solar cap and price. None gives a cycle-life count or the capacity end-point, none gives UPS switchover time, and none separates surge from continuous output. StormWatts says outright that it 'doesn't check usable capacity or cycle life'. Our own 2026-11-04 page has none of these figures either. PowerSized and StormWatts do list solar voltage ranges, but neither says that Jackery's 400 W is two 200 W ports.
decides: This backs the current pick and does not overturn it. The Jackery 1000 v2 was already a lower-ranked card in ChatGPT's answers, and its weaker cycle rating (end-point 70%, not 80%) and 20 ms switchover keep it there. For a shopper backing up a CPAP or a desktop PC, EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic's under-10 ms switchover beats the AC180's 20 ms. That favours the DELTA 3 Classic when the AC180's larger battery (1,152 Wh) isn't what matters. For fridge, lights and Wi-Fi, the order stays as it is.

findings.label: Cycle life and end-point
findings.note: Jackery's own wording is '4000 cycles≥70%'. Anker and BLUETTI rate theirs to 80%, so Jackery's 4,000 is measured to a lower bar and is not directly comparable.

findings.label: Solar input per port vs total
findings.value: 200 W per port (16–60 V, 10.5 A); 400 W only with both ports (21 A)
findings.note: The '400 W max solar input' on spec cards needs two panels on two ports. One 200 W kit panel fills one port completely. A single larger panel on one port is capped at 200 W.

findings.label: Continuous vs surge AC
findings.note: The page also lists '1500W Total For 3 Ports' and AC charging in 'Around 1.7H'.

findings.label: UPS switchover
findings.note: BLUETTI's wording: 'switches over in just 20ms during a power outage'.

findings.label: Surge vs continuous AC
findings.value: 1,800 W continuous; 2,700 W 'Surge Power', which is the same figure as Power Lifting Mode
findings.note: BLUETTI describes the 2,700 W Power Lifting Mode for heating devices. The AC180's surge headroom (2,700 W) is lower than EcoFlow's (3,600 W) or Jackery's and Anker's (3,000 W).

findings.label: Solar input limits
findings.value: 500 W max, Voc 12–60 V DC, 10 A
findings.note: Arithmetic: with a 10 A cap, reaching 500 W needs about 50 V from the panel. A lower-voltage panel is capped at roughly volts × 10 A.
